points.s: The Central Government launched 'Reform Utsav', a nationwide campaign celebrating transformative reforms by ministries and departments, inaugurated by the Prime Minister. Each ministry will hold events showcasing citizen-centric governance and institutional reforms.
points.why: Government schemes and campaigns are staple prelims questions. Note the name, launch date, and stated purpose (reform-oriented governance).

points.s: The Ministry of Panchayati Raj organised special Gram Sabhas across the country on October 2, launching the People's Plan Campaign 2026-27 titled 'Sabki Yojana, Sabka Vikas' for preparing Gram Panchayat Development Plans for 2027-28. Focus areas include Finance Commission grants, eGramSwaraj digital governance, and the SVAMITVA scheme.
points.t: Nationwide special Gram Sabhas; People's Plan Campaign 2026-27 begins
points.why: Panchayati Raj (73rd Amendment, Article 243) is high-weightage in polity. Remember SVAMITVA (property cards for rural households), eGramSwaraj, and the campaign name 'Sabki Yojana, Sabka Vikas'.

points.s: The INDIA bloc announced district-level 'Save Democracy' marches from October 2 to 8, a march of all Opposition MPs to the Election Commission on October 6, and a major Delhi rally on November 1, demanding elections through ballot papers over the SIR (Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls) row.
points.t: INDIA bloc announces 'Save Democracy' march, October 2-8
points.why: Connects to Election Commission (Article 324), electoral roll revision, and EVM vs ballot paper debates, all frequently asked in polity and current affairs sections.

points.s: The Election Commission of India met for the second time in four days and extended the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) dates for Andhra Pradesh and Meghalaya.
points.t: ECI extends SIR dates for Andhra Pradesh and Meghalaya
points.why: SIR is the revision of electoral rolls to remove duplicates and ineligible entries. ECI's powers and the Representation of the People Act, 1950-51 are core polity topics.

points.s: HDFC Bank, India's largest private lender, appointed Anup Bagchi as its next Chief Executive for three years.
points.t: HDFC Bank appoints Anup Bagchi as CEO
points.why: Banking appointments appear in banking-awareness sections. Note the bank (largest private lender) and the three-year term.

points.s: The RRB ALP CBT 2 Result 2026 was declared with zone-wise merit lists and scorecards. Candidates can check their qualifying status for the next stage.
points.why: Directly relevant if you are a railway aspirant. Track result dates and next stages for every exam you target.

points.s: Delhi recorded its most polluted start to October in four years, with AQI settling at 166 (moderate category) on October 1, the highest since 2022's 186, per Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air data.
points.t: Delhi sees most polluted October start in four years (AQI 166)
points.why: Environment current affairs: AQI categories, GRAP (Graded Response Action Plan), CPCB, and stubble-burning season patterns are recurring themes.

points.s: An earthquake of magnitude 4.5 struck Afghanistan. The Hindu Kush region is one of the world's most seismically active zones.
points.why: Geography: the Hindu Kush falls in a convergent plate boundary zone, which is why Afghanistan sees frequent quakes. Map-based questions love this region.

points.s: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal held a productive discussion with US Trade Representative Greer on the early conclusion of the India-US trade deal.
points.t: India-US trade deal talks: Goyal meets USTR Greer
points.why: International relations and economy overlap: trade deals, tariffs, and bilateral mechanisms are standard mains and prelims fodder.

points.s: October 2 is Gandhi Jayanti, the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi (born 1869, Porbandar), observed as the International Day of Non-Violence. It is one of India's three national holidays.
points.why: Static GK that repeats every year: birth year and place, associated movements, and the UN observance (International Day of Non-Violence, adopted 2007).
